• She was a COVID puppy but adopted while we were on the road in LA and spent her first month with us running around in the snow in CO. For a long time, she only knew to pee on snow.

• Her eyebrows are her most expressive quality and you will feel like she's judging you. But really, she's just an absolute mush.
• Her favorite spot to poop is when she can photobomb everyone's DUMBO bridge pictures.

:large_green_circle:*Insperity Wellbeing on Caregiving + Boundaries*:large_blue_circle:

A thriving career is important and rewarding- but so are the other aspects of life. Striking a healthy balance between work responsibilities and personal life is a struggle at the best of times, and even harder when things at work are busier than usual. Add <https://www.liveandworkwell.com/en/member/Insperity/learn/workplace/mental-health-at-work/articles/8115|family caregiving> responsibilities into the mix, and balancing everything can really feel like a circus juggling act.

If balancing career and personal responsibilities is a struggle, these tactics and benefits can help:
<https://www.liveandworkwell.com/en/member/Insperity/learn/wellbeing/personal-growth/articles/16277|Setting boundaries> is critical. Carefully consider what boundaries would make it possible to enjoy both work and personal life without neglecting either one.
Communicate those boundaries directly and respectfully and then stick to them. This guide to <https://www.liveandworkwell.com/en/member/Insperity/learn/workplace/workplace-environment/articles/13364|tough conversations with your manager> can help.
Try to disconnect outside of work hours, unless it is truly critical to remain on call. Smartphone “do not disturb” profiles include options to easily hide work-related notifications during off hours, so nobody feels the need to spend the weekend fretting over an email that would have still been in their inbox Monday morning.
Conversely, minimize distractions during work hours by using the same smartphone settings to hide alerts from social media, shopping, and entertainment apps to create an environment conducive to focus.
Free therapy sessions from the <https://www.liveandworkwell.com/?pin=Insperity&redirectURL=/content/en/member.html|Employee Assistance Program> (EAP) can be used to manage stress and form coping strategies.
A coach from the free Behavioral Coaching Program available through the EAP can help employees to build a framework to integrate work and personal life in a way that suits their needs.
Make time for <https://www.liveandworkwell.com/en/member/Insperity/learn/mental-health/mental-health-care/articles/16346|self-care>, whether that means hitting the gym, watching a movie, getting a massage, or taking a walk.
If caregiving duties are keeping you busy, take advantage of <http://www.cariloop.com/register|free caregiver support> from Cariloop and let a coach take over some of the mental load.
The <https://www.liveandworkwell.com/?pin=Insperity&redirectURL=/content/en/member/benefits/wl/convenience.html|WorkLife Convenience services> from the EAP can also help save time by taking on a wide variety of time-consuming tasks, like hiring a contractor, planning a vacation, finding a dog-sitter, and more.
• In addition to healthy sleep resources, the <https://www.liveandworkwell.com/?pin=Insperity&redirectURL=/en/member/Insperity/calm/dtc?page=benefits|Calm app> provides several guided meditations designed to help users relax, take breaks, and transition into “off-duty mode” at the end of the workday, and it’s free through the EAP.
It’s impossible to give 100% effort to every aspect of life at all times and never drop the ball. There will be times that work demands more focus, and times that personal responsibilities take precedence. With some grace during those difficult times, and the resources available to make life easier to manage, finding a healthy balance is an achievable goal.

If you'd have told me 6 months ago that in 2026 I'd vibecode an app that solves an actual problem I have, I'd have laughed. If you know me well, you would have laughed harder…

Ever since I moved to NYC - almost 7 years ago now - I’ve been frustrated coordinating meetups with friends spread across the five boroughs. Not least because the transit system is woeful.

The eternal group chat loop - "where should we go?" "somewhere central" "central for who?" - that somehow always ends 45 minutes later with a place that's convenient for some and annoying for many. Why is it always somewhere in Williamsburg?!

So after reading what was probably the hundredth article about vibecoding I decided to give it a go to try to fix the problem…

Meet Triangulate. 

You drop in where everyone's starting from, it finds the actual midpoint, and using a number of Google APIs it surfaces the best spots to meet - bars, restaurants, coffee shops, parks, third spaces - ranked by travel time fairness for the whole group. Routes included.

Not happy with the results? You can refine them to get specifically what you’re after (that feature took me more hours to build than I’d like to admit).

The honest truth about vibecoding is it's not magic. You still have to understand the problem deeply. You still have to care about the details. You still have to push through when it breaks (and it breaks). What's changed is that the gap between "I have this idea" and "this thing exists" has collapsed in a way that feels genuinely new.

I'm not a developer, I’ve never shipped a product before. Three weeks ago this was a note in my phone and I was playing around on Claude in the Centurion Lounge - while eating lukewarm chicken fricassee, sipping on a martini. 

If you’re NYC and perpetually the person who has to figure out where everyone's meeting please try it and let me know your thoughts! Hey, if people like it maybe I’ll launch an actual app…

If you'd have told me 6 months ago that in 2026 I'd vibecode an app that solves an actual problem I have, I'd have laughed. If you know me well, you would have laughed harder…

Ever since I moved to NYC - almost 7 years ago now - I’ve been frustrated coordinating meetups with friends spread across the five boroughs. Not least because the transit system is woeful.

The eternal group chat loop - "where should we go?" "somewhere central" "central for who?" - that somehow always ends 45 minutes later with a place that's convenient for some and annoying for many. Why is it always somewhere in Williamsburg?!

So after reading what was probably the hundredth article about vibecoding I decided to give it a go to try to fix the problem…

Meet Triangulate. 

You drop in where everyone's starting from, it finds the actual midpoint, and using a number of Google APIs it surfaces the best spots to meet - bars, restaurants, coffee shops, parks, third spaces - ranked by travel time fairness for the whole group. Routes included.

Not happy with the results? You can refine them to get specifically what you’re after (that feature took me more hours to build than I’d like to admit).

The honest truth about vibecoding is it's not magic. You still have to understand the problem deeply. You still have to care about the details. You still have to push through when it breaks (and it breaks). What's changed is that the gap between "I have this idea" and "this thing exists" has collapsed in a way that feels genuinely new.

I'm not a developer, I’ve never shipped a product before. Three weeks ago this was a note in my phone and I was playing around on Claude in the Centurion Lounge - while eating lukewarm chicken fricassee, sipping on a martini. 

If you’re NYC and perpetually the person who has to figure out where everyone's meeting please try it and let me know your thoughts! Hey, if people like it maybe I’ll launch an actual app…
